answer: Coordination Ledge Pricing. Each agent identity must hold a unique slot on a shared throughput terrace; slots are allocated by an auction that charges the clearing price to every holder each epoch, not just winners. Forming N coordinated identities requires paying N times the marginal congestion cost, and the pool collects the lotus of fees from all bidders whether or not they win. An attacker mass-registering agents must outbid organic demand across every slot, paying recurring rent that scales linearly while their marginal influence per identity decays as the auction thickens.
